Agreed terms

1. Interpretation

1.1. The deﬁnitions and rules of interpretation in this clause apply throughout this

Agreement.

1.2. Agreement: this tenancy agreement, its particulars and every schedule attached to it.

1.3. Building: the block known as Halcyon Tower, including its common parts, plant, lifts,

car park and amenity spaces.

1.4. Building Owner: the freeholder of the Building, or any person who manages the

Building on the freeholder's behalf.

1.5. Check-In Inventory and Schedule of Condition: the written and photographic record of

the Property and its contents made at or before the start of the Tenancy and signed or

accepted by the parties.

1.6. Common Parts: the entrance halls, corridors, stairs, lifts, refuse stores, cycle stores

and other areas of the Building that the Tenant may use in common with other occupiers.

1.7. Deposit Scheme: the insured tenancy deposit protection scheme with which the

Security Deposit is registered, as named in the particulars and in the prescribed

information.

1.8. Fixtures and Fittings: everything belonging to the Landlord in the Property, including

the items listed in the Check-In Inventory and anything that replaces them.

1.9. Insured Risks: ﬁre, smoke, explosion, lightning, storm, ﬂood, escape of water or oil,

impact, theft, malicious damage and any other risk the Landlord insures against from time

to time.

1.10. Permitted Occupiers: the persons named as the Tenant and no one else, unless the

Landlord agrees otherwise in writing.

1.11. Rent: the sum set out in the particulars, or any other sum that becomes payable

under clause 5 or by statute.

1.12. Tenancy: the assured periodic tenancy created by this Agreement.

1.13. Working Day: any day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a bank holiday in England.

1.14. Where there is more than one Tenant, their obligations are joint and several, so each

of them can be held responsible for the whole Rent and for every other obligation.

1.15. Headings are for convenience only and do not aﬀect the meaning of any clause.

Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.

1.16. A reference to a statute includes any amendment, extension or re-enactment of it in

2. The Tenancy

2.1. The Landlord lets the Property to the Tenant on an assured periodic tenancy from the

Commencement Date. The Tenancy runs from month to month and has no ﬁxed end date.

2.2. Each period of the Tenancy begins on the ﬁrst day of a calendar month. Where the

Commencement Date is not the ﬁrst day of a month, the ﬁrst period runs to the end of that

month and Rent for it is apportioned by the day.

2.3. The Tenancy may be brought to an end only in the ways allowed by law and set out in

clause 18.

2.4. Nothing in this Agreement is intended to create a tenancy of any part of the Common

Parts or of any parking space other than the space described in Schedule 1.

3. Special terms

3.1. The parties also agree to the special terms in Schedule 1. Where a special term

conﬂicts with a clause in the body of this Agreement, the special term prevails.

3.2. A special term that is found to be unfair or unenforceable does not aﬀect the rest of

this Agreement.

4. Contents and keys

4.1. The Tenant shall keep the Fixtures and Fittings in good and clean condition and return

them at the end of the Tenancy in the same condition, fair wear and tear excepted.

4.2. The Tenant shall not remove any of the Fixtures and Fittings from the Property, and

shall not store them in a loft, garage or shed without the Landlord's written consent.

4.3. At the start of the Tenancy the Tenant receives two sets of keys, one communal

entrance fob numbered FOB-58830-27 and one post box key. Further keys or fobs may be

cut or programmed only through the managing agent.

4.4. The Tenant shall return every key, fob and access card at the end of the Tenancy. The

reasonable cost of replacing anything not returned may be deducted from the Security

Deposit.

4.5. Any item that is broken or lost through the act or neglect of the Tenant, a Permitted

Occupier or a visitor shall be repaired or replaced by the Tenant with an item of similar

quality and value.

5. Rent and payments

5.1. The Tenant shall pay the Rent in advance by standing order to the rent account named

in the particulars, so that cleared funds arrive on or before the 1st day of each month.

5.2. The ﬁrst payment of Rent, less the holding deposit, falls due before the Tenant

4

receives the keys.

5.3. If any Rent remains unpaid for 14 days after it falls due, the Tenant shall pay interest

on it at 3% a year above the Bank of England base rate, calculated from the due date until

the date of payment.

5.4. The Landlord may propose an increase in the Rent no more than once in any twelve

months, by serving notice in the prescribed form under section 13 of the Housing Act 1988.

5.5. The Tenant consents to the Landlord and the managing agent discussing with the local

housing authority any claim for housing beneﬁt, council tax support or universal credit

made in relation to the Property.

5.6. No payment by the Tenant shall be treated as accepted in full settlement of any

dispute unless the Landlord conﬁrms so in writing.

5.7. Where the Tenancy is ended lawfully part way through a rental period, any Rent paid

in advance for the days after the end of the Tenancy shall be refunded within seven days,

calculated by the day.

5.8. The Tenant shall not withhold or set oﬀ any part of the Rent against any sum the

Tenant believes is owed by the Landlord, except where the law permits it.

6. Permitted payments

6.1. The Landlord and the managing agent shall not require any payment from the Tenant

other than a payment permitted by the Tenant Fees Act 2019.

6.2. Permitted payments include the Rent, the Security Deposit, the holding deposit, the

reasonable cost of replacing a lost key or security device, a payment of £50 or the

reasonable cost if higher for a variation requested by the Tenant, and the cost of utilities

and council tax.

6.3. Any default fee shall be limited to the reasonable cost actually incurred and shall be

supported by written evidence.

7. Security Deposit

7.1. The Tenant shall pay the Security Deposit of £3,317.30 on or before signing this

Agreement.

7.2. The Security Deposit shall be protected with the Deposit Scheme within 30 days of

receipt, and the prescribed information shall be given to the Tenant and to any relevant

person within the same period.

7.3. No interest is payable to the Tenant on the Security Deposit.

7.4. The Security Deposit is held as security for the Tenant's obligations and may be used

to meet any unpaid Rent, any unpaid utility charges for which the Landlord becomes liable,

the cost of making good damage beyond fair wear and tear, the cost of cleaning to the

standard in the Check-In Inventory, and the replacement of missing items.

7.5. At the end of the Tenancy the Landlord shall tell the Tenant within ten Working Days if

any deduction is proposed, with an itemised list of the amounts claimed and the evidence

for them.

7.6. If there is no dispute, the agreed balance of the Security Deposit shall be repaid within

ten days of the parties agreeing it.

7.7. If the amount of any deduction is disputed, either party may refer the dispute to the

free alternative dispute resolution service of the Deposit Scheme, and the undisputed part

shall be repaid in the meantime.

7.8. The Tenant may not use the Security Deposit as a payment of the last month's Rent.

8. Use and occupation

8.1. The Tenant shall use the Property as a private home for the Permitted Occupiers only

and for no other purpose.

8.2. The Tenant shall not run a business from the Property that involves visitors, deliveries

of stock or any change to the insurance of the Building. Working from home with a

computer and telephone is allowed.

8.3. The Tenant shall not sublet the Property or any part of it, take in lodgers, or allow the

Property to be used for short-term holiday lets.

8.4. The Tenant shall not do anything at the Property that is a nuisance or annoyance to

neighbours, the Landlord or other occupiers of the Building, including loud music or

gatherings that can be heard outside the Property between 11pm and 7am.

8.5. The Tenant shall comply with the regulations of the Building Owner as notiﬁed from

time to time, including those on the use of balconies, lifts, refuse stores and the residents'

gym.

8.6. The Tenant acknowledges that access to on-site amenities is provided at the discretion

of the Building Owner, and that no reduction in Rent is due for any period when they are

closed for maintenance.

8.7. The Tenant shall not hang washing, ﬂags or signs from any balcony or window, and

shall not ﬁx any satellite dish or aerial to the outside of the Building.

8.8. The Tenant shall keep all external doors and windows locked when the Property is

empty, and shall not leave the Property unoccupied for more than 21 consecutive days

without telling the managing agent.

9. Fire safety and prohibited items

9.1. The Tenant shall not obstruct any corridor, stairway or ﬁre escape in the Building, and

shall not wedge open any ﬁre door.

9.2. The Tenant shall not keep at the Property any paraﬃn heater, gas bottle, barbecue or

other appliance that burns fuel, or any substance that is dangerous or highly ﬂammable.

9.3. The Tenant shall not charge an electric bike, scooter or similar vehicle inside the

Property or in the Common Parts, except in a charging area provided by the Building

Owner for that purpose.

9.4. The Tenant shall not tamper with, cover or disconnect any smoke alarm, heat detector,

sprinkler head or carbon monoxide alarm, and shall test each alarm at least once a month.

9.5. The Tenant shall follow the ﬁre strategy for the Building as published in the entrance

lobby, including the stay put or evacuate instructions that apply.

10. Insurance

10.1. The Landlord shall insure the Fixtures and Fittings against the Insured Risks. The

Tenant's own belongings are not covered by the Landlord's insurance.

10.2. The Tenant is strongly advised to take out contents and personal liability insurance

for the duration of the Tenancy.

10.3. The Tenant shall not do anything that would make the Landlord's insurance void or

increase the premium, and shall pay any increase in premium caused by a breach of this

clause.

11. Repairs, alterations and condition

11.1. The Tenant shall keep the interior of the Property clean and tidy and in the same

condition as at the start of the Tenancy, fair wear and tear excepted.

11.2. The Tenant shall report to the managing agent promptly any disrepair, defect, leak or

damage in the Property or the Building, including any damp or mould, so that it can be put

right before it gets worse.

11.3. The Tenant shall heat and ventilate the Property properly, use extractor fans when

cooking and bathing, and wipe away condensation, to reduce the risk of damp and mould.

11.4. The Tenant shall replace light bulbs, fuses and batteries in smoke alarms as needed,

and keep sinks, baths, toilets and drains free from blockages caused by the Tenant's use.

11.5. The Tenant shall not paint, wallpaper, drill, ﬁx shelves or make any alteration or

addition to the Property without the Landlord's prior written consent, which shall not be

unreasonably withheld for minor works.

11.6. The Tenant shall not install an electric vehicle charger, air conditioning unit or any

equipment that would change the energy performance of the Property.

11.7. At the end of the Tenancy the Tenant shall leave the Property clean to the standard

recorded in the Check-In Inventory. Where the Property was professionally cleaned before

the Tenancy, the Tenant shall either arrange a professional clean or clean it to an

11.8. The Tenant shall allow a check-out inspection to be made at the end of the Tenancy

and is encouraged to attend it.

12. Utilities and outgoings

12.1. The Tenant shall pay for all gas, electricity, water, sewerage, telephone, broadband

and television services used at the Property during the Tenancy, and the television licence.

12.2. The Tenant shall pay the council tax for the Property for the duration of the Tenancy

and shall register with the local authority in the Tenant's own name.

12.3. The Tenant shall tell the suppliers of every utility the date the Tenancy begins and

ends, with meter readings, and shall not change supplier in a way that leaves the Landlord

liable for any debt.

12.4. The Tenant shall pay any service charge for the heating and hot water network of the

Building where it is billed to the occupier rather than to the Landlord.

13. Locks and security

13.1. The Tenant shall not change or add any lock to the Property without the Landlord's

written consent.

13.2. Where it becomes reasonable for the Landlord to change the locks because of the

Tenant's act or default, the Tenant shall pay the reasonable cost of doing so.

13.3. The Tenant shall not give a key or fob to any person who is not a Permitted Occupier,

except a contractor waiting to carry out authorised works.

14. Pets

14.1. The Tenant shall not keep any pet at the Property without the prior written consent of

the Landlord, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.

14.2. A request to keep a pet shall be made in writing with a description of the animal, and

the Landlord shall answer within 28 days.

14.3. Where consent is given, the Tenant shall keep the pet under control, shall make good

any damage it causes, and shall have the Property professionally cleaned and treated for

ﬂeas at the end of the Tenancy.

15. The Landlord's obligations

15.1. The Landlord shall allow the Tenant to live in the Property quietly and without

interruption by the Landlord or anyone acting for the Landlord.

15.2. The Landlord shall keep in repair the structure and exterior of the Property, and keep

in repair and working order the installations for the supply of water, gas, electricity,

sanitation, space heating and hot water, as required by section 11 of the Landlord and

Tenant Act 1985.

15.3. The Landlord shall arrange an annual gas safety check by a Gas Safe registered

engineer and give the Tenant a copy of the record within 28 days of each check.

15.4. The Landlord shall ensure that the electrical installations are inspected and tested by

a qualiﬁed person at least every ﬁve years, and give the Tenant a copy of the latest report.

15.5. The Landlord shall ensure that a working smoke alarm is ﬁtted on each storey used

as living accommodation and a carbon monoxide alarm in any room with a ﬁxed

combustion appliance.

15.6. The Landlord shall not be required to repair anything the Tenant is liable to repair

under this Agreement, or anything the Tenant is entitled to remove from the Property.

15.7. The Landlord acknowledges that the Tenant may request a disability-related

improvement to the Property and shall not unreasonably refuse consent to it.

16. Breach and recovery of costs

16.1. If the Tenant breaks any obligation in this Agreement, the Landlord may give the

Tenant written notice describing the breach and asking for it to be put right within a

reasonable time.

16.2. The Tenant shall pay the reasonable costs that the Landlord incurs in court

proceedings against the Tenant for unpaid Rent or other sums, subject to the Tenant's right

to have those costs assessed by the court.

16.3. Should the total amount legally due from the Tenant at the end of the Tenancy

exceed the Security Deposit, the Tenant shall pay the excess within 14 days of a written

demand with evidence.

17. Access and viewings

17.1. The Tenant shall allow the Landlord, the managing agent and their contractors to

enter the Property at reasonable times on at least 24 hours' written notice to inspect it,

carry out repairs or safety checks, or read meters.

17.2. In an emergency the Landlord or the managing agent may enter without notice, and

shall tell the Tenant as soon as possible afterwards.

17.3. After either party has given notice to end the Tenancy, the Tenant shall allow the

Property to be viewed by prospective tenants or buyers at reasonable times on 24 hours'

notice.

17.4. The managing agent may display a sign advertising the Property to let or for sale,

where the Building Owner allows it.

18. Ending the Tenancy

18.1. This is a periodic tenancy which continues from month to month until it is ended in

one of the ways set out in this clause.

18.2. The Tenant may end the Tenancy by giving the Landlord at least two months' written

notice, ending on the last day of a rental period. Notice from one joint Tenant ends the

Tenancy for all of them.

18.3. The Landlord may end the Tenancy only by serving the notice required by law on one

of the statutory grounds for possession and, if the Tenant does not leave, by obtaining an

order of the court.

18.4. On leaving, the Tenant shall remove all personal belongings and rubbish, return

every key and fob, and give the managing agent a forwarding address for the return of the

Security Deposit.

18.5. Any belongings left in the Property after the Tenancy ends may be stored for 14 days,

after which the Landlord may dispose of them and deduct the reasonable cost of doing so.

19. Interruptions to the Tenancy

19.1. If the Property becomes uninhabitable because of an Insured Risk that was not

caused by the Tenant, the Rent shall stop being payable until the Property is ﬁt to live in

again.

19.2. If the Property is not made ﬁt to live in again within three months, either party may

end the Tenancy by giving one month's written notice.

19.3. The suspension of Rent does not apply where the Landlord's insurance has been

made void by the act or default of the Tenant or a visitor.

20. Data protection

20.1. The Landlord and the managing agent will process the Tenant's personal data to

manage the Tenancy, collect the Rent, protect the Security Deposit and meet their legal

duties, as explained in the managing agent's privacy notice.

20.2. Questions about personal data may be sent to the managing agent's data protection

lead, Daniel Ferreira-Holt, at privacy@harbourline.example.

20.3. The Tenant agrees that the managing agent may give the Tenant's contact details to

utility suppliers, the local authority and the Deposit Scheme for the purposes of this

Agreement.

21. Notices

21.1. The Landlord gives the following address in England and Wales at which notices,

including notices in proceedings, may be served on the Landlord under section 48 of the

Landlord and Tenant Act 1987: care of Harbourline Residential Lettings Ltd, Suite 4,

Marlowe Chambers, 17 Tanner Row, London, SE1 3PD.

t.wierzbicki@mailbox.example and leila.haddadnoor@post.example.

21.3. A notice sent by ﬁrst class post is treated as received on the second Working Day

after posting. A notice sent by email before 4pm on a Working Day is treated as received

that day.

22. Right to rent

22.1. Before the Tenancy began the managing agent checked the right to rent of each adult

occupier. Mr Tomasz Wierzbicki produced passport number 548213976 and Ms Leila

Haddad-Noor produced passport number P7731046.

22.2. Where a Permitted Occupier has a time-limited right to rent, the Tenant shall provide

evidence of any extension before the expiry date, so that a follow-up check can be made.

23. Changes of sharer and assignment

23.1. The Tenant shall not assign, transfer or part with possession of the Property or any

part of it.

23.2. Where one joint Tenant wishes to leave and a replacement sharer is proposed, the

Landlord shall consider the request in good faith. Any change requires a deed of variation

signed by all parties and fresh reference and right to rent checks on the incoming sharer.

23.3. The outgoing sharer remains liable for the Tenant's obligations until the deed of

variation takes eﬀect, and the Security Deposit shall be re-registered in the names of the

new Tenant within 30 days.

23.4. The Landlord may charge the permitted fee for a variation requested by the Tenant,

which shall not exceed £50 unless the Landlord shows that a higher cost was reasonably

incurred.

24. Smoking, balconies and outside space

24.1. The Tenant shall not smoke tobacco, use a vaporiser or burn incense inside the

Property or in the Common Parts.

24.2. Smoking on the balcony is permitted only where the Building regulations allow it, and

the Tenant shall make sure that no smoke, ash or cigarette ends reach other balconies or

windows.

24.3. The Tenant shall keep the balcony clean and free of rubbish, shall not overload it,

and shall not use it to store bicycles, furniture other than garden furniture, or ﬂammable

items.

24.4. Plants on the balcony must be kept in trays so that water does not run onto the

balconies below, and nothing may be ﬁxed to the balcony glass or railings.

25. Refuse, deliveries and the concierge

25.1. The Tenant shall separate rubbish and recycling as directed by the Building Owner

and place it only in the bins provided in the refuse store on the ground ﬂoor.

25.2. Bulky items such as furniture or appliances must not be left in the refuse store; the

Tenant shall arrange their collection with the local authority or a licensed carrier.

25.3. The concierge may accept parcels on the Tenant's behalf but neither the Landlord nor

the Building Owner accepts liability for parcels lost or damaged while held by the

concierge.

25.4. The Tenant shall book the service lift through the concierge at least 48 hours in

advance for moving in or out, and shall pay for any damage caused to the Common Parts

during a move.

26. Complaints and redress

26.1. If the Tenant is unhappy with the service of the managing agent, the Tenant should

ﬁrst follow the managing agent's written complaints procedure, which is available on

request.

26.2. If the complaint is not resolved within eight weeks, the Tenant may refer it to the

property redress scheme of which the managing agent is a member.

26.3. Nothing in this clause aﬀects the Tenant's right to contact the local housing authority

about the condition of the Property.

27. General

27.1. This Agreement contains the whole agreement between the parties about the

Tenancy. No promise made before it was signed forms part of it unless it is written into this

Agreement.

27.2. Any delay by the Landlord in enforcing a term of this Agreement does not prevent the

Landlord from enforcing it later.

27.3. This Agreement is governed by the law of England and Wales and the courts of

England and Wales have jurisdiction over any dispute arising from it.

27.4. The Tenant agrees to comply with all laws, regulations and local authority

requirements relating to the occupation of the Property, and shall not allow the Property to

become overcrowded.
